findings: Buys: over the five trading days from the fill, the stocks it bought beat SPY by 0.66% on average (68 buys, 59% of them ahead of SPY; t = 1.9, within noise).
Sells: over the five trading days from the fill, the stocks it sold beat SPY by 0.38%, so selling gave that up (120 sells; t = -1.4, within noise).
Decision IC: on the 34 days it traded, what it bought ranked against what it sold and left alone by a mean rank IC of 0.010 with the next five days' returns (IC IR 0.08, t = 0.5, within noise).
Holdings IC: the weights it held after each of 45 decision days had a mean rank IC of -0.023 with the next five days' returns (t = -1.2, within noise).
Factor exposures: market 0.30 (t 7.4), size -0.09 (t -2.1), growth 0.11 (t 1.6), momentum 0.02 (t 0.4); together they explain 62% of the daily variation (R²).
Of the +2.5% a year it earned over T-bills (arithmetic mean): market +6.3%, growth +2.6%, size -0.5%, momentum +0.3%; the alpha left is -6.3% a year (t = -0.8, within noise).
Verdict: most of the return is factor exposure (+8.8% a year, market above all); the alpha left is not significant.
P&L: +$2,094 in all, +$1,982 from 55 positions and +$112 of interest on idle cash.
By holding period: 61+ days made the most (+$4,085, 6 positions); 11-20 days the least (-$5,142, 12 positions).
By sector: Technology made the most (+$5,071, 11 positions); Utilities the least (-$2,727, 2 positions).
By stock: TMO made the most (+$1,607, 2 positions); NEE the least (-$2,727, 2 positions).
By market regime of the previous close: risk-on 26 days -2.7% (SPY -4.3%); uncertain 142 days +7.4% (SPY +14.2%); risk-off 85 days -2.3% (SPY +7.2%).
News: 22 positions opened on news made -$218, the other 33 +$2,200; 14 positions closed on news made +$900; over the five days from the fill, news-triggered buys beat SPY by 1.13% (t 2.0).

Concentration: the gains are spread out (the best two positions made 16% of them) but winners and losers nearly cancel, so the best two made 132% of the net P&L; the best was TMO bought 2020-05-06 and sold 2020-08-14, +$1,531. Had the best position made nothing, the run would have returned +0.6% instead of +2.1%.
